record.statement: Does a decomposable forward Brownian motion which is also backward Brownian necessarily become two-sided Brownian after a random shift? The source also asks weaker related formulations using independence of past and future at a random time.
record.statement_caveat: The three linked formulations are grouped as one compatibility problem. A general process that is both forward and backward Brownian without the extra assumptions is already counterexampled in the paper.
record.title: Compatibility of forward and backward Brownian decompositions

record.independent_check: Independence of two halves at a proposed joining time is insufficient if their Brownian marginal laws have been lost there.
record.obstruction: No construction aligns both certificates at one time while preserving both marginal laws and their independence.
record.result: Two independent standard Brownian half-paths attached at the same deterministic time give a two-sided Brownian motion. For a general process certified separately as forward and backward Brownian, the certifying random times can differ. Moving either certificate to another random time can bias its marginal law, as the selection-density calculation in P0032 demonstrates.

store_cards.title: Attempt on Compatibility of forward and backward Brownian decompositions
store_cards.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Common-splice compatibility obstruction Result: Two independent standard Brownian half-paths attached at the same deterministic time give a two-sided Brownian motion. For a general process certified separately as forward and backward Brownian, the certifying random times can differ. Moving either certificate to another random time can bias its marginal law, as the selection-density calculation in P0032 demonstrates. Check: Independence of two halves at a proposed joining time is insufficient if their Brownian marginal laws have been lost there. Obstruction: No construction aligns both certificates at one time while preserving both marginal laws and their independence.
